01. Have you attached your transcripts for all completed units or degrees? Options: Yes | No | Not Applicable

Administers District employee and retiree health and welfare benefit programs, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, and other assigned benefit programs.

Administers benefit enrollments, changes, terminations, and continuation-of-coverage processes for employees, retirees, and eligible dependents in accordance with applicable collective bargaining agreements, Board policies, plan documents, and legal requirements.

Coordinates new-employee benefits orientation and enrollment; explains benefit options, eligibility requirements, enrollment procedures, and general terms and conditions of employment-related benefits.

Responds to inquiries from employees, retirees, dependents, departments, and the public regarding benefits eligibility, enrollment, qualifying life events, leave-related benefits, retirement-related information, and related procedures; provides information within the area of assignment and refers detailed coverage or claim questions to the appropriate carrier or administrator.

Plans, coordinates, and administers the annual open-enrollment process; prepares employee communications, reviews enrollment materials for completeness and accuracy, coordinates with carriers and administrators, and resolves enrollment-related issues.

Maintains accurate benefit enrollment, eligibility, dependent-verification, leave, and retiree records in applicable human resources and benefits systems; protects confidential information and ensures timely and accurate processing of records and transactions.

Prepares and reconciles insurance eligibility reports, carrier invoices, premium statements, payroll-deduction information, and related financial records; researches and resolves discrepancies with carriers, administrators, employees, retirees, and District departments.
Tracks and processes retiree medical and dental benefit payments and related records; provides retirees with timely information regarding coverage, status, required actions, and plan changes.

Maintains information and communications regarding health and welfare benefits, retirement programs, plan descriptions, and related forms through the District’s designated employee communication channels.
Prepares, distributes, and maintains required benefits notices and communications; monitors applicable deadlines and time requirements for benefits-related entitlements and reporting.
Coordinates, audits, and processes annual Affordable Care Act reporting, including IRS Form 1095-C; prepares audit reports, tracks employee work hours as required, and maintains supporting records.

Compiles, reviews, and provides active-employee and retiree data for required actuarial valuation and other benefits-related reporting; prepares financial, statistical, and narrative reports, summaries, surveys, and recommendations related to benefits administration.
Maintains enrollment and related records for tax-sheltered annuity programs and coordinates information with appropriate providers and District departments.

Receives, reviews, and processes initial work-related injury and illness reports, including incident reports and DWC-1 forms; submits claim files to the District’s workers’ compensation third-party administrator or carrier within required deadlines.

Serves as a primary District contact for injured employees and supervisors regarding the initial workers’ compensation reporting process; coordinates with the appropriate District departments, third-party administrators, carriers, and medical providers as assigned.

Assists employees with leave-related benefits documentation and processes, including FMLA/CFRA and disability-related forms; coordinates with employees, supervisors, and District departments regarding benefit continuation and required documentation during approved leaves.

Conducts research, analyzes data, and prepares clear written, statistical, and oral reports and recommendations on benefits issues; assists with benefit studies, surveys, and related planning activities.

Provides courteous and effective customer service in person, by telephone, and through written and electronic communication; resolves routine concerns in an efficient and timely manner and escalates complex matters as appropriate.
Attends and participates in professional meetings and training; maintains current knowledge of benefits administration trends, regulations, and procedures.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Operations, services, and activities of employee and retiree benefits programs.
Perform professional benefits administration work with minimal supervision and exercise sound independent judgment.
Principles and procedures related to employee benefits compliance, including Affordable Care Act reporting, COBRA, FMLA/CFRA, and OPEB actuarial reporting requirements.
Interpret and apply plan documents, collective bargaining agreements, Board policies, administrative procedures, and applicable laws and regulations to benefits eligibility and administration.
California public retirement frameworks and tax-sheltered annuity programs.
Collect, compile, audit, reconcile, and analyze benefits, financial, and statistical information and data.
Principles and practices of insurance eligibility reporting, premium reconciliation, benefits billing, financial record keeping, and actuarial data preparation.
Prepare complete and accurate reports, notices, correspondence, analyses, and recommendations.
Basic workers’ compensation reporting requirements, injury-reporting timelines, and claims-administration workflows.
Coordinate multiple benefits activities, meet critical deadlines, and adapt to changing priorities.
Methods and techniques for research and analysis of personnel, financial, and statistical data.
Audit complex benefit rosters; identify and resolve discrepancies with carriers, administrators, employees, retirees, and District departments.
Applicable collective bargaining agreements, Board policies, plan documents, and federal, state, and local laws, codes, regulations, and reporting requirements related to benefits administration.

Explain complex benefit, leave-related benefit, retirement-related, and enrollment information clearly, tactfully, and empathetically to employees, retirees, dependents, supervisors, and department representatives.
Principles and practices of customer service, confidentiality, business letter writing, and report preparation.
Respond tactfully, clearly, concisely, and appropriately to sensitive inquiries from the public, District staff, carriers, and other agencies.
Office procedures, methods, equipment, and computer applications, including word processing, spreadsheet, database, enterprise resource planning, and human resources information systems.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Exercise good judgment and maintain confidentiality in handling sensitive information, records, and reports.

Principles, practices, and procedures of benefits administration, including enrollment, eligibility, premium administration, retiree benefits, disability, leave-related benefits, and workers’ compensation reporting.
Communicate and interact effectively in situations requiring tact, instruction, persuasion, and counseling, including individual interviews, group discussions, and presentations.
Health and welfare benefit plans, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, and continuation-of-coverage programs.
Operate office equipment and supporting word processing, spreadsheet, database, and human resources information systems.

Demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students and staff.
